winners.premise: A groom replaces the bride's name with his late wife's in the wedding vows and tells the officiant she has agreed without asking her.
winners.conflict: A bride must make room for her partner's grief without agreeing to disappear into the identity of the woman he lost.
winners.twist: The supposed tribute requires the living bride to answer to another woman's name, and correcting the script cannot by itself make the groom ready to marry her.
winners.hook: My groom changed my name to his late wife's in our wedding vows. He'd told the officiant I'd agreed, but he'd never asked me.
winners.narration: At the rehearsal, Helen checked the name against the card I'd brought with my spelling on it. Helen said Paul had told her I'd agreed. Paul asked whether we could leave the other version in because hearing another name beside his felt like losing Anna again. I said we could honor her without calling me Anna. He told Helen I was nervous and would feel differently tomorrow. I asked him to stop answering for me. He said a few words shouldn't matter if I knew he loved me. But he wasn't asking for a few words about her. He wanted me to stand where she'd stood and answer when he used her name. Helen put the script down. His mother asked what had happened. He said I wanted Anna left out of the wedding. I explained what he'd asked me to do. She said that wasn't what remembering Anna had to mean. Paul finally used my name and asked whether we could just start again. I said saying it once didn't settle why he'd thought I should give it up. We stopped the rehearsal and postponed the ceremony. I wasn't asking him to forget his wife. I needed him to know who he was marrying. I put my name card back in my bag. If we tried again, I was bringing it with me.
winners.title: The Name Card Beside Their Wedding Vows
winners.description: The officiant reads a different name in the wedding script. The groom has agreed to the change on behalf of the woman he plans to marry.
winners.payoff: If we tried again, I was bringing it with me.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HER OWN NAME MATTERS

winners.premise: A husband admits throwing away his wife's father's ashes so he can use the urn for coins, then offers to buy a replacement container.
winners.conflict: A woman must face an irreversible loss when her husband treats her father's ashes as clutter and offers money instead of acknowledging what he discarded.
winners.twist: The rubbish has already been collected, so another urn can replace only the container, not what her husband decided she should stop keeping.
winners.hook: My husband admitted throwing my dad's ashes away to use the urn for coins. Then he offered me money for a new one.
winners.narration: I heard the coins when I moved it to dust the shelf. Mark said he'd emptied it on Tuesday because I never used it for anything. I asked what he'd done with the ashes. He said he'd put them in the rubbish, which had been collected that morning. I went outside anyway. The bin was empty. When I came back, he said he'd pay for a new urn, even a nicer one. I told him I wasn't upset about losing a ceramic pot. He said keeping ashes in the living room only made me sad, and he'd thought it might help me move on. I asked when he'd decided my grief was something he could clear out while I was at work. He said he couldn't undo it, so I needed to tell him what would make it right. I didn't have an answer he could buy. My sister called while he was still offering replacements. I told her what had happened. Mark asked why I was involving everyone in a private mistake. I said they were her dad's ashes too. She offered to come over, but I asked whether I could stay with her instead. I emptied the coins into a bowl and took the urn with me. Mark said it was empty now. I knew. That was the part he kept expecting another purchase to fix.
winners.title: The Coins Inside Dad's Urn
winners.description: He thinks buying another urn can fix what he has thrown away. His wife is grieving something that cannot be reordered.
winners.payoff: That was the part he kept expecting another purchase to fix.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF SOME LOSSES CANNOT BE REPLACED

winners.premise: A mover locks a customer's furniture in his truck after she refuses a date, while his coworker tells her to agree and cancel once the delivery is complete.
winners.conflict: A woman must recover her furniture when a delivery worker treats access to her new home and belongings as leverage for a date.
winners.twist: Her apparent agreement is an attempt to get the paid delivery finished, and she withdraws it once her belongings are inside.
winners.hook: My mover locked my furniture in his truck because I refused to date him. His coworker told me to say yes and cancel later.
winners.narration: Dave carried in three boxes, then asked me to dinner. I said no, thanks, and pointed out where the table should go. He closed the truck instead. I asked him to finish the paid delivery. He said I could be nice back. His coworker Neil quietly told me one dinner wasn't a big promise. I asked whether he'd unload. He said Dave was the driver and I was holding both of them up. I was standing outside my new flat with the rest of my things locked away. So I said we could discuss dinner after the furniture was inside. Dave asked whether that meant yes. I said yes. He opened the truck and started carrying things again. Neil gave me a smile like he'd solved the problem. I didn't smile back. Once the last box was inside, Dave asked what time he should collect me. I told him I wasn't going to dinner. He said I'd made a promise. I said he'd made a paid delivery depend on getting one. I wasn't discussing my evening with him again. They left, and I called the company to report exactly what had happened, including what I'd said to get my things back. I didn't know what they would do about it. That evening, I ate at my own table. I'd only needed him to deliver it.
winners.title: The Dinner He Added to the Delivery
winners.description: The furniture is still in the truck when the driver decides dinner with the customer should be part of the arrangement.
winners.payoff: I'd only needed him to deliver it.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF DELIVERY DOES NOT BUY A DATE

winners.premise: A boss lets his six-year-old daughter cancel an employee's approved day off and makes the employee explain why his son's school play matters more than her birthday party.
winners.conflict: An employee must hold his adult boss responsible when the boss uses a child's pretend management role to reverse an approved family commitment.
winners.twist: The daughter does not understand that her birthday wish is being used as a real employment decision and hands responsibility back to her father.
winners.hook: My boss let his six-year-old cancel my approved day off. He said I could explain to her why I was missing her birthday party.
winners.narration: Gary's daughter Mia sat at his desk with a manager badge and a flower stamp. My leave form was underneath it. Gary had approved the afternoon for my son's school play. Now he said Mia had decided she needed me at her party instead. I asked whether he was changing it. He pointed at her and said I should respect the manager's answer. Mia told me there would be cake and that she wanted me to help put up the balloons. I told Gary I wasn't arguing about my leave with a child. He said I was spoiling her fun. Mia asked whether my son was having a party too. I said he was in a play, and I'd promised to be there. She asked her dad whether he'd miss her birthday if someone stamped no on his paper. Gary said this was different. She took off the badge and handed him my form. She said she'd only wanted me to come, and he should tell me if I couldn't go to the play. I asked him again, without asking her. He finally admitted he'd expected me to help set up the party and agreed I could keep the afternoon off. Mia put the badge back in her toy box. She went back to stamping flowers on paper. I went to my son's play.
winners.title: The Flower Stamp on His Leave Form
winners.description: The boss calls his daughter the manager when she rejects an employee's leave. She has not been told what her pretend job is actually deciding.
winners.payoff: I went to my son's play.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF DAD SHOULD ANSWER HIMSELF
